text: **SECOPS-21 remains open. Symptom:** security-ops follow-up 10 (#265) saw first post-restore offer generation `11` while the node retained `14`, despite #245's floor over `nodes.desired_config_generation`, `nodes.applied_config_generation` and stored desired-state history. Older offers raise `ErrStaleGeneration`. **Rule (D-095, #270):** stop control/worker, restore T0, and freeze-ingest before starting either service on the restored database. The compiler holds the first post-restore compile until a fresh observation from the current incarnation arrives after `usage_ledger_state.mode` left `normal`. The observable hold is `pending fresh observation after restore` (retryable `503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, node drift `desired_state_restore_observation`, operation step `fresh_observation`). **Verification:** after a fresh applied `14` report, require first new offer `15`, node acceptance without `ErrStaleGeneration`, then a separate applied ACK and converged `config_generation.desired` / `config_generation.applied`. Completing recovery alone must not release the hold. D-099 is fixed at the HTTP layer in wire-nodes follow-up 29 (#277). `CompileTx` always proposes `max(desired, applied, stored)+1`; cache reuse is allowed for the cached generation or its ordinary one-step proposal only when no higher applied/stored generation exists and no restore observation is outstanding. Policies follow-up 8 (#286) promotes `TestAT30_D095_HTTPRestoreCacheProbe`: the exact 503 hold precedes offer `15` above retained `14`; the pre-#277 negative control fails with `304 / generation 11`. The fixture ACKs are simulated. Do not close SECOPS-21 from the compiler tests alone. Live closure requires the first delivered offer, a matching node-local accepted envelope/ETag, successful application and a separate real applied ACK; absence of a stale-generation log is insufficient. See the [HTTP fix note](../nodes/2026-10-31-secops-21-handover.md) and [live closure checklist](../policies/2026-10-31-secops-21-handover.md).

Installer ENR-06 (#266) historically failed first start because `/var/run/netbird.sock` was outside the packaged write allowlist and consumers could remove shared runtime state. Installer follow-up 3 (#279) fixes this: the daemon owns `/run/fvpn-netbird/netbird.sock` and shared `/run/vpn-node` survives consumer restarts. Offline seed and firstboot now pass with real daemons, but the required full journaled upgrade stays **red** at the absent meter checkpoint (`final_sample`, `CHECKPOINT_FAILED`, health null). Do not infer success from updater exit 0. See [installer follow-up 3](../node/install-followup3-2026-10-31.md). Devstack follow-up 15 remains historically `21 pass / 1 fail`; enrollment follow-up 6 (#288) now verifies ENR-06 startup on the fixed installer (AT06 376/0/0, AT07 26/5/0). Five AT07 rows remain blocked on installer-node exports and ENR-05; startup success does not close the full upgrade test. Updates follow-up 9 passed regular AT23–AT27 on `5575470`, while its separate installer extension remains blocked on measured F9-01…F9-05; [current dispositions](../ops/README.md#follow-up-15-acceptance-snapshot-2026-10-31-edt).

D-095's exact fresh-observation hold is proved. SECOPS-21 remains open: the
first probe/stored generation 16 exceeds retained 15, but first delivery,
matching local acceptance and the applied ACK remain unproven; capture is
pending devstack follow-up 18 / wire-nodes follow-up 32. Earlier measurements
remain historical, and no candidate-hardware guarantee follows. See the
[current acceptance snapshot](../ops/README.md#follow-up-16-acceptance-snapshot-2026-10-31-edt).

1. **`fvpn-usage-admin freeze --reason "AT30 restore drill"`** (with `fvpn-control` and `fvpn-worker` stopped): set `usage_ledger_state.mode = 'frozen'` (`0.08 s`).
  2. **`fvpn-usage-admin begin-recovery --reason "AT30 restore to T0" --checkpoint-at "2026-10-30T22:07:20.427256Z" --key-id <recovery-key-id> --private-key-file <recovery.key>`**: rotated `ledger_epoch` (`7232c191-6989-4246-be92-cf0d74a15091` -> `31fa2c6f-a685-4919-92b4-41bf7614c158`), created `usage_recovery_records` (`130fd33b-5da0-4051-9bd9-5d2859a49c2f`), recomputed `usage_checkpoints` watermarks (`highest_contiguous_seq = 2`), and entered `mode = 'reconciling'` (`0.11 s`).
  3. **Start `fvpn-control` and `fvpn-worker` so retained nodes reconcile and replay**: `node1` received `409 LEDGER_EPOCH_MISMATCH`, fetched the signed checkpoint from `GET /api/v1/agent/usage-checkpoint`, verified its Ed25519 signature, un-archived locally retained `seq=3..5` (`archived=1 -> 0`), and replayed `seq=1..6` (`seq=1..2` `duplicate`, `seq=3..6` `accepted`) — **`5/5` (`T0..T1`) events replayed with `5/5` canonical SHA-256 matches, `0` lost, `0` double-counted, `0` gaps (`gap=false`)**, reducing service usage RPO from the **`116.651 s`** (`T1 - T0`) database window to **`0 s`**.
  4. **`fvpn-usage-admin complete-recovery --recovery-id 130fd33b-5da0-4051-9bd9-5d2859a49c2f`**: marked recovery `completed`, cleared `reconciliation_in_progress`, and returned `usage_ledger_state.mode` to `'normal'` (`0.09 s`).

**SECOPS-19 closure:** during the reconciling hold, `node_observations.report_payload.usage` reported `unacked_event_count = 3` and `unacked_payload_bytes = "2352"`; `fvpn-agent usage snapshot -json` reported `unacked_count = 3` and the same payload bytes. After complete-recovery and replay both reached zero events and `"0"` bytes. Billing reconciliation converged the canceled member to expired entitlement with one refund; the other member remained active without an entitlement extension. SECOPS-05 also closed in this run.
